findings: The actual diagnostic150 never sets full_instantaneous_circle_admitted or physical_metric_admitted true. It displays selected radial-balance speeds with all geodesic defects; the one-sided vertical defect is not its sole unqualification gate.
Sampler93 explicitly uses positive-side reflected Q1 normal jets and the reflection tensor Q=diag(1,1,-1,1). At the sheet the odd normal metric/time cross entries vanish by the original masks.

For a tangent circle W=(1,0,0,Omega), reflection gives Gamma_minus^a_bc=Q_a Q_b Q_c Gamma_plus^a_bc. Tangential contractions and the full dynamic radial/time/axial equations agree on both sides; the normal coordinate acceleration changes sign. A reflection-mean representative therefore has zero normal acceleration and the same radial candidate speed.

A nonzero positive-side normal acceleration tests a bulk worldline on that side. Requiring it to vanish is an additional restriction, and cannot by itself refute a reflection-symmetric thin-sheet circle. The norm alone supplies neither its restoring sign nor a stability test.

For the existing particle/ordinary canonical action H=N E-beta dot p, restricting a worldline to the sheet yields tangential Euler-Lagrange equations from the induced metric. A normal support/reaction or symmetric regularization must be declared and derived from the matter/junction problem; neither is supplied by these diagnostic sources. Unrestricted variation through a cusp requires a declared weak/regularized junction prescription rather than an arbitrary single-sided derivative.

The saved rotating-sheet source independently retains radial Euler and angular-momentum contacts while physical_junction_qualified remains false. It does not establish the distributional normal junction or a complete material history.

A mean/intrinsic sheet interpretation could change the circle-compatibility meaning without changing the 43 radial speeds. It cannot promote the nonconverged metric, failed canonical/constraint gates, or unqualified readout precision to physical acceptance. Persistent orbit stability and line-of-sight/reduced observational translation remain separate requirements.

A new independent parity control can check equal tangential circle coefficients and opposite normal forces for the two supplied jet limits; a mean-sheet normal zero is a symmetry identity, not a solved junction or stability certificate.
